exposure: synthetic MRI metrics (T1, T2 relaxation times, and Proton Density values) in different brain regions (frontal white matter and caudate)
outcome: neurodevelopmental outcomes (disability status, cognitive and motor outcome scores)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 80 extremely preterm neonates diagnosed with low-grade Germinal Matrix-Intraventricular Hemorrhage (GMH-IVH).
finding: Synthetic MRI, particularly the combined model of T1 and T2 relaxation times in frontal white matter and caudate, effectively predicts adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes in extremely preterm infants with GMH-IVH.
